clue.text: Interview sought by players

explanation.surface: Someone is asking for a meeting with a group of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interview' reads as a job chat, but here it is the formal meeting granted by a monarch or pope.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal interview with a dignitary, and also the crowd that performers seek out.

clue.text: Doctor in last throes, nearly

throes are violent spasms, so the word last is convulsed into a new order

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is at the patient's side as they come close to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throes' turns LAST into ALST, and 'in' puts MO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean all but, very close to completely.

clue.text: A girl's career in communication

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so a girl's gives DI'S
a career is a course through life

explanation.surface: A young woman's working life is spent in communications.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is talk or written exchange of ideas, a form of communication.

clue.text: Cats lie all over the place, being adaptable

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of cats lie are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cats sprawl everywhere, fitting themselves to any spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic stretches and yields, so it is flexible in the way it adapts.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying journalist — one based in Lebanon

indicators.note: the vehicle holds the journalist within it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A car transports a reporter, who is stationed in Beirut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one based in Lebanon' suggests a foreign correspondent; it is the tree on Lebanon's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar of Lebanon is the country's national tree, rooted there.

clue.text: Mean fellow who refused initially to eat out

indicators.note: the opening letters of who and refused are taken

parts.note: to etch is to eat out a surface with acid

explanation.surface: A stingy man turned down an invitation to dine at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy; it means wretched, low.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a despicable, miserable person, a low fellow.

clue.text: Get better, as a retriever might

explanation.surface: A gundog improves its performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain health, and a retriever's job is to fetch back shot game.

clue.text: Belonging to those folk in that place, say

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: there means in that place

explanation.surface: Something owned by people over there.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive of they, showing something owned by those people.

clue.text: A large number rely wrongly on its accommodation

definitions.text: A large number rely wrongly on its accommodation

parts.note: a host is a great crowd

indicators.note: the letters of rely are set in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Many people mistakenly depend on the lodging offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' turns RELY into ELRY, after HOST; the whole clue pictures guests counting on an inn's rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an inn, a place offering lodging to many guests.

clue.text: Being under eighteen, starts to respect young soldiers

parts.note: in law a minor, under eighteen, is an infant

indicators.note: the first letters of respect and young are taken

explanation.surface: Teenage recruits are expected to show respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young soldiers' looks like a single phrase, but 'young' gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers collectively.

clue.text: Child's toy is a duck with nothing inside

indicators.note: the zero sits within the bird's name

parts.note: the scoter is a sea duck
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A toy duck is hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a duck' suggests a rubber bath toy; it is the scoter, a sea duck. 'with nothing inside' puts O within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is a two-wheeled plaything a child pushes along with one foot.

clue.text: Unfavourable notice introducing literary composition

indicators.note: the notice comes first, leading into what follows

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
verse is poetic writing

explanation.surface: A bad review greets a new piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or harmful, working against someone.

clue.text: Blunt criticism of loyal person by striker

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, loyal friend
a bat is something that strikes a ball

explanation.surface: A faithful supporter is harshly criticised by a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer; it is a bat. A BRICK is old British slang for a dependable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is an unkind remark, a hostile comment hurled like a missile.

clue.text: Native darts champions rely on it

definitions.text: Native darts champions rely on it

parts.words: Native darts champions rely on it
parts.note: reads like pub darts players and their kit, but means hunters in the forest firing darts by breath

explanation.surface: Top local darts players depend on a piece of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which indigenous hunters puff darts at prey.

clue.text: Advert in palindromic form

indicators.note: the answer reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An advertisement written so it reads the same both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' looks like an advertisement; it is the verb meaning to mention or allude.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is to allude to or mention it.

clue.text: Convicts inside often made to break up rock

indicators.note: the convicts go within the scrambled word
the word often is broken up and reassembled

parts.note: lags is slang for convicts

explanation.surface: Prisoners are frequently set to breaking rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to break up' turns OFTEN into FTONE, and 'inside' puts LAGS within it. 'inside' also hints at prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is a flat slab of stone used for paving.

clue.text: Late drink going to one's head?

explanation.surface: An evening drink goes to a person's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink before bed, and also a cap worn on the head while sleeping.

clue.text: Standard job description uttered by a stockjobber

definitions.text: job description uttered by a stockjobber

explanation.surface: A trader states what his normal work involves.
explanation.walkthrough: A stockjobber was a dealer on the London Stock Exchange, so he might say 'I deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection, and a stock trader describing his job says he deals.

clue.text: Party held in rented quarters — a disappointment

indicators.note: the party is enclosed by the other letters

parts.note: let means rented out
W and N are two quarters of the compass, west and north
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party in hired rooms turns out to be a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A letdown is an anticlimax that fails to meet hopes.

clue.text: Main ploy confounded Zeus, for one

indicators.note: the letters of main ploy are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: A chief scheme baffled the king of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was one of the gods of Mount Olympus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Birds to pluck set out

parts.note: to pull is to pluck

indicators.note: out signals the word set disordered

explanation.surface: Poultry are laid out ready for plucking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pullets are young hens.

clue.text: Trading area encountered in, vessel? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
the reverse of the order stated: the vessel goes inside, not the other way

parts.note: met means encountered
an ark is a vessel, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A market is found aboard a ship, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'encountered in vessel', and 'On the contrary' flips it: ARK goes inside MET.
explanation.definitionFit: A market is a place where goods are bought and sold.

clue.text: The high point for students appearing in popular opera

indicators.note: the students are placed inside the next word

parts.note: a hit is something popular
L is a learner, so two students give LL
OP is short for opus or opera

explanation.surface: The best moment for students is seeing a well-liked opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilltop is the summit, the highest part of a hill.

clue.text: Motorway. enclosed by, illuminated boundary

indicators.note: the motorway letter is surrounded by the other word

parts.note: lit means illuminated
Motorway gives MI

explanation.surface: A lit-up motorway marks the edge of an area.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a bound or edge beyond which one may not go.

clue.text: Musical instrument? Rosalind's cousin is in Paris replacing one

indicators.note: the French word takes the place of the numeral one

parts.note: Celia is Rosalind's cousin in Shakespeare's As You Like It
I is the Roman numeral one
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A question about an instrument, then a Shakespearean heroine's relative turns up in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates.

clue.text: Professorship in church music

parts.note: an air is a tune, music

explanation.surface: An academic post in sacred music.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a professor's post at a university.

clue.text: But surely not a low grade volume?

definitions.text: But surely not a low grade volume?

parts.words: But surely not a low grade volume?
parts.note: reads as a protest that a book cannot be second-rate, because its name calls it ordinary and a book

explanation.surface: Someone objects that a book cannot really be inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonplace book is a notebook of collected quotations and jottings.

clue.text: One in hospital is missing one, that's clear

indicators.note: the second word drops out of the first

parts.note: a patient is someone in hospital
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hospital patient has gone missing, which is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means obvious or plain to see.

clue.text: Street getting bigger?

explanation.surface: A road appears to be growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is a curved road of houses, and crescent once meant increasing, as a waxing moon.
